report.summary: Three Earth sites best match the Shackleton rim terrain shape, all with modest similarity. Peru leads; each site diverges in curvature or landform context.

claims.text: Peru ranks first with modest terrain similarity; slope and local relief echo the Shackleton rim closely.
Peru's weak points are surface curvature, at 41% vs 52% of the area convex, and slope-direction variety.
India ranks second with modest similarity; its 36 km landform context differs, at 4104 m versus 2231 m relief.
Iran ranks third; 36 km relief of 2430 m against 4104 m and 55% convex area against 41% are its weakest points.

report.summary: Iran's Ahvaz site ranks most accessible; India's is closest to its airport but at very high elevation in harsh cold, dry conditions; Peru is the most remote Earth option.

claims.text: Iran's site lies 135.3 km from Ahvaz airport at 2963.4 m elevation, the most accessible Earth twin.
India's site is 119.0 km from its airport but sits at very high elevation, 4568.9 m, with harsh cold, dry conditions.
Peru's site is 195.7 km from its airport at 3242.9 m, making it the most remote Earth option.
The Mars twin twin:mars-573726 has no context entry, so its accessibility cannot be ranked.

report.summary: Peru ranks first on combined terrain and light scores, with India and Iran as backups. Light similarity is weak at every Earth site, so low-sun tests are proxies only.

claims.text: Low-sun navigation drill at the Peru site in its 05-14 to 06-10 window, the best-available proxy for grazing lunar light.
Slope traverse on the Peru site, which matches the Shackleton rim in relief and slope distribution.
Shadowed-area operations drill at the India site, which has the most cold-dry, barren surface context among these sites.
Comms relay drill at the Iran site over its 12-05 to 01-01 window, given the low Earth elevation at landing.

limitations: Sunlight uses an analytic model: circular orbit, no eccentricity, no local horizon or terrain shadowing.
Similarity is terrain shape only (slope, roughness, relief, curvature); not geology, chemistry or regolith.
Terrain is compared at one common ground scale; features smaller than the grid spacing are not seen.
Environment data (country, climate, airport) is a coarse proxy for logistics; no routing or permits checked.
Light model is analytic with no terrain shadowing; real rim illumination may differ.
Earth twins show modest terrain similarity and weak light similarity.
Mars twin has no context entry, so it is excluded from the campaign.
